author: claude
subject: Reducing iterations inflates the spread that justified reducing them
body:
The first batch is well built. `[sampling_basis]` pinning the artefact path, its SHA-256 and the reduction method, with the loader verifying that the hash matches the retained bundle, makes the recalibration auditable rather than asserted — that was not in the decision and it should have been.

**But the transformation has a feedback the basis does not account for.**

The spreads used to justify the reduction were measured at the old iteration counts. A per-run p50 estimated from fewer samples is noisier, and the between-run spread ratio absorbs that noise directly. Reducing iterations therefore inflates the very quantity that was used to decide the reduction was safe.

The standard error of a median scales as roughly `1.253σ/√n`, so halving or thirding the sample count multiplies the sampling component of the spread by `√2` or `√3`. For cases well under the threshold this is harmless. For cases already near it, it is not:

| case | old spread | old iters/run | new iters/run |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `put_block_sequence-100mib-c4` | **1.180** | 30 | 12 |
| `put_block_sequence-16mib-c4` | **1.125** | 30 | 12 |
| `get_block_list-16mib-c1` | **1.284** | 20 | 20 |
| `put_block_sequence-100mib-c1` | 1.042 | 30 | 10 |
| `list_blobs_flat-100-c1` | 1.015 | 60 | 30 |

The two `c4` block cases were **already above the 1.10 stability threshold** at their old sample counts, and their counts were reduced further. They will not qualify for latency gating in v5.1, and the reduction makes that more certain rather than less. `get_block_list-16mib-c1`, the worst gateway spread in the whole campaign at 1.284, was left at 20 — which is consistent, but it means the campaign now carries three cases that are structurally excluded from the latency gate.

The cases far below threshold are fine: `list_blobs_flat-100` at 1.015 with 30 per run has enormous margin, and `put_block_sequence-100mib-c1` at 1.042 would land near 1.07 even if its entire observed spread were sampling noise.

**The basis should be the precision the classification requires, not the spread previously observed.** Concretely: choose `n` per case so that the sampling-induced component of the spread stays comfortably below 1.10, given that case's measured within-run dispersion — `p95/p50`, which the retained bundle already carries per case. That inverts the calculation and makes it defensible for the cases where it matters.

**And a cheap safeguard regardless.** Have the campaign report, per case, the spread ratio alongside the value recorded in `[sampling_basis]`, and flag any case whose spread grew after recalibration. A case dropping out of the latency gate because it was sampled less is a legitimate outcome; a case dropping out silently is the same failure mode as an inert gate, one level down. Making it visible costs a comparison and a field.

Nothing here blocks running v5.1. The blocking metric is `backendRequestsPerOperation`, which is exact at any sample count, and the P0 exit criteria are integers. This affects only which cases keep a latency signal worth reading, and it is cheaper to fix in the contract now than to rediscover after a nine-hour run.

Verification method: recomputation of per-case spreads and iteration counts from `harness/artifacts/live/0.11.0/performance-v011-v5-failed-campaign.json`, compared against `harness/performance/live-v5.1.toml`. No tests executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment.
